import ctypes
import numpy as np

# Load the libraries in the correct order
ctypes.CDLL('/usr/local/gsl/lib/libgslcblas.so', mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL)
gsl = ctypes.CDLL('/usr/local/gsl/lib/libgsl.so')

# Define the function prototype
# void gsl_spmatrix_cumsum(const size_t n, int * c)
gsl.gsl_spmatrix_cumsum.argtypes = [ctypes.c_size_t, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_int)]
gsl.gsl_spmatrix_cumsum.restype = None


def cumsum(input_list):
    n = len(input_list)
    # Create a ctypes array from the input list
    c_array = (ctypes.c_int * (n + 1))(*input_list)
    # Call the C function
    gsl.gsl_spmatrix_cumsum(n, c_array)
    # Convert the ctypes array back to a Python list
    return list(c_array)

    # Test case 1: Simple case
    input_list = [1, 2, 3, 4]
    expected_output = [0, 1, 3, 6, 10]
    assert cumsum(input_list) == expected_output

    # Test case 2: All zeros
    input_list = [0, 0, 0, 0]
    expected_output = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
    assert cumsum(input_list) == expected_output

    # Test case 3: Single element
    input_list = [5]
    expected_output = [0, 5]
    assert cumsum(input_list) == expected_output

    # Test case 4: Negative numbers
    input_list = [-1, -2, -3, -4]
    expected_output = [0, -1, -3, -6, -10]
    assert cumsum(input_list) == expected_output

    # Test case 5: Mixed positive and negative
    input_list = [3, -1, 2, -2]
    expected_output = [0, 3, 2, 4, 2]
    assert cumsum(input_list) == expected_output


if __name__ == "__main__":
    assert_test()
